To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Compromised Recognition Of Turnip Crinkle Viruses (CRV1) subfamily of micorochida ATPases (MORC) are negative regulators of plant immunity.

MORC1 and 2, two of seven GHKL ATPases of Arabidopsis thalianan, regulate multiple aspects of plant immunity and that the barley MORC homologs have opposing functions in plant immunity compared with Arabidopsis.
barley MORCs function as modulators in plant immunity and can act negatively (decrease resistance) or positively (increase resistance) in different species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the barley MORC proteins in plant immunity.
the function of the Compromised Recognition Turnip Crinkle virus1 subfamily of the microrchidia (MORC) superfamily of GHKL domain-containing ATPases in barley.
the identification and characterization of barley MORC proteins and their function in plant immunity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the function of MORC proteins in plant immunity is highly species dependent.
the function of MORCs in plant immunity is species dependent.
MORCs are not involved in the silencing of transposable elements, but rather are involved in plant immunity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MORC proteins have evolved a novel function in plant immunity.
the barley MORC1 homologue functions as a negative regulator of immunity, which contrasts to the function of AtMORC proteins in Arabidopsis.

barley MORCs negatively regulate disease resistance, while AtMORCs positively regulate disease resistance, suggesting a novel layer of plant immunity that may be exploited in breeding for enhanced disease resistance in barley and other cereals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the role of MORC proteins in disease resistance is species-specific.
the function of MORC proteins in plant immunity is conserved, but the directionality of their function is not.
the same protein in different plant species can function in opposite ways in plant immunity.
